executive_summary: Five recent exploitable vulnerabilities and library flaws covering Linux kernel race conditions, perimeter device input validation, CMS remote file inclusion, JWT parsing DoS, and Angular SSR DoS. Each offers concrete defensive learning opportunities for portfolio projects in systems, network, web, and secure coding domains.

signals.title: Linux Kernel contains a race condition vulnerability which allows concurrent writes to the same AF_ALG socket causing data to be unpredictably interleaved and creating inconsistenc
signals.what_changed: Race condition in AF_ALG socket handling permits interleaved writes, corrupting internal state.
signals.why_it_matters: Can lead to information leakage or privilege escalation in containerized workloads that rely on AF_ALG for cryptographic operations.
signals.application: Study kernel hardening, eBPF-based monitoring, and namespace isolation; build a lab to detect abnormal socket behavior.

signals.title: Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway contain an improper input validation vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands.
signals.what_changed: Improper input validation in NetScaler ADC/Gateway permits unauthenticated remote code execution.
signals.why_it_matters: Critical perimeter device flaw; exploitation can compromise entire DMZ and pivot internally.
signals.application: Deploy a vulnerable NetScaler instance in a isolated lab, test input sanitization, and evaluate WAF or IDS signatures.

signals.title: WordPress Core contains a remote file inclusion vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to make page-template resolution include a chosen readable local `.php`
signals.what_changed: RFI via page-template resolution allows inclusion of arbitrary local .php files outside theme directory.
signals.why_it_matters: Widely deployed CMS; unauthenticated RCE enables full site compromise and server takeover.
signals.application: Set up a WordPress test site, verify input validation on template parameters, and test security plugins or mod_security rules.

signals.title: PyJWT: Unauthenticated RecursionError DoS in pre-verification payload parse (PyJWKClient.get_signing_key_from_jwt / verify_signature=False)
signals.what_changed: Recursion error triggered when parsing JWT payload with verify_signature=False, causing denial of service.
signals.why_it_matters: Applications that disable signature verification for debugging or legacy reasons can be crashed by crafted tokens.
signals.application: Review JWT handling code, enforce strict validation, add payload size limits, and test with malformed tokens.

signals.title: Angular Server-Side Rendering (SSR): Denial of Service via Numeric URL Matrix Parameters
signals.what_changed: Excessive numeric matrix parameters in URLs cause resource exhaustion during Angular SSR rendering.
signals.why_it_matters: SSR applications can be overwhelmed, leading to service degradation or crash.
signals.application: Test an Angular SSR app with crafted URLs, implement request validation and parameter limits, monitor CPU/memory usage.

experiment.title: Detect AF_ALG socket race condition using eBPF tracing
experiment.objective: Identify abnormal concurrent writes to AF_ALG sockets in a controlled environment and generate alerts via eBPF.
prerequisites: A test program that opens AF_ALG sockets and performs concurrent writes (can be a simple C/Python script)
steps: 1. Compile and run the test program that spawns multiple threads writing to the same AF_ALG socket.
2. Attach an eBPF tracepoint to sock_alloc_send_skb or similar kernel function to count write operations per socket.
3. Log occurrences where write count exceeds a threshold within a short time window.
4. Correlate logs with test program timestamps to confirm race condition detection.
5. Optionally, apply a kernel patch or configure socket options to mitigate and observe reduced alerts.
expected_evidence: eBPF output showing spikes in write counts per AF_ALG socket during test execution
Correlation of spikes with the test program's concurrent write phases
Reduction or elimination of spikes after applying a mitigation (e.g., using socket locking or updated kernel)
experiment.stop_condition: When consistent evidence of race condition is observed and mitigation verification is complete, or after 30 minutes of active tracing.

discarded: Other items were excluded due to overlap in theme (multiple Citrix flaws), lower practicality for short lab work, or lack of clear defensive exercise path.
